coordinates.note: Surveyed midpoint of the MINOS far detector (between its two supermodules), NAD 83; the paper quotes an inertial survey good to 0.7 m per coordinate.
coordinates.quote: That midpoint was surveyed and determined to be located at latitude 47.820267 degrees north, longitude 92.241412 degrees

depth.quote: The detector is housed in a specially excavated cavern, 705 m underground (2070 meters-water-equivalent)

muon_flux.display: 1.65 × 10⁻⁷ cm⁻² s⁻¹ (± 0.02 stat., ± 0.1 syst.), E > 1 GeV
muon_flux.locator: Abstract and Sec. IV (Muon and neutron measurements at Soudan Mine), Eq. (5), Phys. Rev. D 90, 122003 (arXiv:1407.3246)
muon_flux.note: Muon flux through a horizontal surface for muon energies above 1 GeV, from 655.1 days of a 12-litre liquid-scintillator detector operating in the Soudan Mine; the paper does not say it stood in the MINOS cavern, whose depth (2070 m.w.e.) is the one recorded here. The paper also quotes 1.77 × 10^-7 cm^-2 s^-1 from the MINOS far detector. Mei & Hime Table I gives (2.0 ± 0.2) × 10^-7 cm^-2 s^-1 at 1.95 ± 0.15 km.w.e., from a thesis. Woodley et al. 2024 call the 1.65 × 10^-7 result the only peer-reviewed Soudan measurement they know. The quote's factor 10^-7 multiplies the whole bracket, so the stored value is 1.65 × 10^-7 cm^-2 s^-1 with no unit conversion. The paper gives the depth of the Soudan laboratory as 690 m (2100 m.w.e.).
muon_flux.quote: The muon flux is found to be (1.65 ± 0.02(sta.) ± 0.1(sys.)) × 10−7 cm−2 s−1 (Eµ > 1 GeV)

summary.plain: The purpose-built cavern half a mile underground in the old Soudan iron mine that held the MINOS far detector, 735 kilometres from the neutrino beam that was aimed at it.
summary.technical: Excavated hall on the 27th level of the Soudan mine at 705 m depth (2070 m.w.e.), 735.3 km from the NuMI production target, which housed the 5.4 kt magnetised MINOS far detector.
